answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Bridging. Each identity gets a persistent behavioural fingerprint (topic mix, timing, counterpart set) from a seed period, then every later epoch must match within a tolerance window; a garden of fresh unlinked identities is rejected because new keys lack matching histories. Similarity is measured on signed interaction graphs, with a jetty threshold for acceptable drift. An attacker must maintain each identity's fingerprint across many epochs, hitting an economic nadir where per-identity upkeep exceeds any single-epoch payoff.
